edges.act_citation_note:
NO INSTRUMENT WAS LOCATED, AND ONE IS BELIEVED TO EXIST. A reprint described as
EMENDED was emended by someone; the 2002 book records the state and not the act.

This station is drawn because omitting it would make a postconciliar recension
silently wrong about 1971 to 1975, and the omission would be invisible: the
missal acquisition audit found this reprint by READING a leaf rather than by
searching, and recorded that a record omitting it `will be silently wrong`.

The value is `not-found` and NOT `none-claimed`, and the difference is the whole
point of having both. A `printed` station claims no act at all; this one says an
act is missing.

The date is `1971` with `date_precision = "year"`, which is what the leaf gives.
No day is invented to make it sort.
edges.act_citation_scope:
ADDED 2026-08-01, when `check` began requiring a not-found to name what was
searched (guidance/act-histories.md section 10, item 2). The bound is stated
from what this record can support and no more.

Searched: THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN SOURCE LIBRARY, for `reimpressio`, which returns
fifteen files. They are this slice, four other inventories, one calendar, the
2008 Variationes work and its Notitiae edition, a segment record of the 2002
typical edition, and a work record for the 2008 NOTICE of the emended reprint --
that is, records ABOUT the reprint and none of the reprint's own instrument.

NOT searched: the Acta Apostolicae Sedis for 1971, Notitiae for 1971, and the
front matter of any 1971 printing. Not found here means not in the tree and not
in the witnesses this slice declares. It is not a statement about any archive.
edges.parent_basis:
The 2002 typical edition's own printing-history leaf lists the states of the
book in order, and this reprint is the second of them. The edge rests on the
book's list, not on an instrument, which is what `book-states-it` means.
